newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to replace Dutch pork due to swine fever.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to replace Dutch pork due to swine fever.

text.p: South Korea will re-invite tenders to replace Dutch pork previously purchased due to an outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands, traders and officials said on Thursday.
A total of 4,616 tonnes of Dutch pork is expected to be substituted for other origins including 2,740 tonnes in a government tender and !,876 tonnes bought by the Simultaneous-Buy-Sell group.
Swine fever broke out in the North Brabant province of the southern Netherlands in early February and the Dutch authorities have since started a massive pig cull to contain the disease.

Officials with the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry said South Korea had bought a total of 14,422 tonnes of pork since early January as a part of a government plan to buy 20,000 tonnes to ease domestic prices. Out of the total purchase, Dutch pork took 2,740 tonnes -- 800 tonnes for shipment in March and 1,940 tonnes for shipment in April.
They said the purchase plan was in addition to the country's obligation to buy 14,620 tonnes this year under the Minimum Market Access (MMA) requirement of the World Trade Organisation.
A ministry official said the Simultaneous-Buy-Sell group had so far bought 3,582 tonnes of Dutch pork to meet this year's quota under the MMA agreement.
"According to the agreement between the Netherlands and South Korea, South Korea's imports of Dutch pork slaughtered by February 2 have already been halted," the ministry official told Reuters.
Lasy year, South Korea's pork imports totalled 38,392 tonnes including its MMA amount of 23,392 tonnes.
South Korea has said it would open its pork market from July this year.
